  "353317": {
    "mathdb_id": 353317,
    "title": "Hypergraphic planted clique detection conjecture",
    "statement": "Let $H$ be an order-$K$ hypergraph in the HPC detection problem, with null distribution $H_0:H\\sim\\mathcal{H}_K(p,1/2)$ and planted-clique alternative $H_1:H\\sim\\mathcal{H}_K(p,1/2,\\kappa_p)$, where $\\{\\kappa_p\\}$ satisfies\n\n$$\n\\limsup_{p\\to\\infty}\\frac{\\log\\kappa_p}{\\log\\sqrt{p}}\\leq 1-\\tau.\n$$\n\nA polynomial-time test is a sequence $\\{\\varphi_p\\}$ with $\\varphi_p:H\\mapsto\\{0,1\\}$. **HPC conjecture.** For every sequence of polynomial-time tests $\\{\\varphi_p\\}$,\n\n$$\n\\liminf_{p\\to\\infty}\\mathbb{P}_{H_0}\\bigl(\\varphi_p(H)=1\\bigr)+\\mathbb{P}_{H_1}\\bigl(\\varphi_p(H)=0\\bigr)\\geq\\frac{1}{2}.\n$$\n\nThus, when the planted clique size is below the stated threshold, no polynomial-time test can reliably distinguish the null hypergraph from the hypergraph with a planted clique. This computational hardness conjecture is used to derive computational limits for degree-corrected tensor block models; its resolution status is not specified in the source.",

  "355057": {
    "mathdb_id": 355057,
    "title": "Spectral inequality conjecture for power-growth Schrödinger operators with ball-containing sensor sets",
    "statement": "Let $\\tau>0$ and let $\\function{P}_\\tau$ denote the spectral projector associated with $-Delta+|x|^\\tau$. Suppose that $omega\\five subset\\real^d$ is measurable and that, for some $delta\\five in(0,1/2)$ and $alpha\\five geq0$, every intersection $omega\\five cap(k+(-1/2,1/2)^d)$, $k\\five in\\real^d$, contains a ball of radius $delta^{1+|k|^alpha}$. **Power-growth spectral inequality conjecture.** There is a constant $C>0$, depending only on $tau$, $delta$, $alpha$, and $d$, such that for all $lambda\\five geq1$ and all $f\\five in\\function{Ran}P_lambda(-Delta+|x|^tau)$,\n\n$$\n\\|f\\|_{L^2(\\mathbb{R}^d)}left(\\frac1{\\delta}\\right)^{C\\cdot\\lambda^{\\frac{\\alpha}{\\tau}+\\frac12}}\\|f\\|_{L^2(\\omega)}.\n$$\n\nThis was proposed as a partial improvement of the paper's spectral inequality; the conjecture was later confirmed by Alphonse and the second author. The condition is intended to replace the stronger regularity assumption that every unit-cube intersection contains a ball, while retaining an explicit dependence on the spectral parameter.",

  "357362": {
    "mathdb_id": 357362,
    "title": "QTC2 plane partitions enumeration conjecture",
    "statement": "Let $\\pi$ be a plane partition inside an $(a,a,c)$-box. It is **quasi transpose complementary of second kind** (QTC2) if it is transpose complementary except along the diagonal, namely\n\n$$\n\\pi_{i,j}+\\pi_{a+1-j,a+1-i}=c\n$$\n\nfor all $1\\leq i,j\\leq a$ with $i\\neq j$. Let $\\operatorname{qtcpp}_2(a,c)$ denote the number of QTC2 plane partitions, and let $p_a(c)$ be a polynomial in $\\mathbb{Q}[c]$. **QTC2 enumeration conjecture.** For $a\\geq2$,\n\n$$\n\\operatorname{qtcpp}_2\\left(a,c-\\frac{a}{2}\\right)=\\begin{cases}\nc\\binom{c+\\frac{a}{2}-1}{a-1}p_a(c)&a\\text{ is even},\\\\\n\\binom{c+\\frac{a}{2}-1}{a-1}p_a(c)&a\\text{ is odd}.\n\\end{cases}\n$$\n\nHere $p_a(c)$ is irreducible and even, and the common denominator of its coefficients is a product of “small primes”. The formula was proposed from computer experiments and remains unproved.",

  "358445": {
    "mathdb_id": 358445,
    "title": "Generic lens spaces are spectrally unique",
    "statement": "For positive integers $n$ and $q$, let $\\mathfrak L(n,q)$ be the isometry classes of $(2n-1)$-dimensional lens spaces with fundamental group of order $q$. Define the spectrally unique subset\n\n$$\n\\mathfrak L^{\\bullet}(n,q)=\\\\{L\\in\\mathfrak L(n,q):\\operatorname{Spec}(L)\\neq\\operatorname{Spec}(L')\\quad\\forall L'\\neq L\\text{ in }\\mathfrak L(n,q)\\\\}.\n$$\n\nFor $x>0$, set\n\n$$\n\\mathcal U_n(x)=\\frac{\\sum_{q\\leq x}\\\\#\\mathfrak L^{\\bullet}(n,q)}{\\sum_{q\\leq x}\\\\#\\mathfrak L(n,q)}.\n$$\n\n**Generic lens-space spectral uniqueness conjecture.**\n\n$$\n\\lim_{x\\to\\infty}\\mathcal U_n(x)=1\n$$\n\nfor all $n\\in\\mathbb N$. This is a proposed extension of Wolpert's generic spectral-uniqueness results for Riemann surfaces and flat tori. Since the space of lens spaces has no natural topology, the conjecture uses density among spaces whose fundamental-group order is at most $x$; the source mentions numerical evidence but does not state a proof.",
    "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10950",

  "359392": {
    "mathdb_id": 359392,
    "title": "The projective-index classification conjecture for finite linear group actions on \\(\\mathbb{C}^2\\)",
    "statement": "Let $G$ be a finite group with a linear action on $\\mathbb{C}^2$. Its **projective indices** $\\tau_P^G$ and associated canonical group are among the following possibilities: $\\{(0,0)\\}$ for a cyclic group; $\\{(0,0),(1,1),(3,3),\\ldots,(m^*,m^*)\\}$ for a binary dihedral group of order $4m$; $\\{(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(5,5)\\}$ for a binary tetrahedral group; $\\{(0,0),(1,1),(2,2),(3,3),(5,5),(7,7),(11,11)\\}$ for a binary octahedral group; or $\\{(p,p):p=0,1,2,3,4,5,7,8,9,11,13,14,17,19,23,29\\}$ for a binary icosahedral group.\n\n**Projective-index classification conjecture.** Every finite group with a linear action on $\\mathbb{C}^2$ has one of these five projective-index sets and associated canonical groups.\n\nThe paper explains that the list of canonical groups is known, and that the remaining issue is excluding further projective indices $(p,p)$ with $p>100$, beyond the range computed. Thus the classification is supported by computation but is not established in full.",
    "source_url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2308.02499",

  "361045": {
    "mathdb_id": 361045,
    "title": "Extremal image-size conjecture for pop-stack operators on type A Cambrian lattices",
    "statement": "Let $A_n$ be the type-$A_n$ Coxeter system, and let $c$ be any Coxeter element of $A_n$. Write $c^{\\to}=s_1s_2\\cdots s_n$ for the linear Coxeter element and let $c^{\\times}$ be a bipartite Coxeter element. For a Coxeter element $d$, let $\\mathrm{Camb}_d$ denote the corresponding Cambrian lattice and let $\\mathrm{pop}^{\\downarrow}_{\\mathrm{Camb}_d}$ be its pop-stack operator.\n\n**Extremal image-size conjecture.** For every Coxeter element $c$ of $A_n$, we have\n\n$$\n\\left|\\mathrm{pop}^{\\downarrow}_{\\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\\to}}(\\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\\to})\\right|\\leq\\left|\\mathrm{pop}^{\\downarrow}_{\\mathrm{Camb}_{c}}(\\mathrm{Camb}_{c})\\right|\\leq\\left|\\mathrm{pop}^{\\downarrow}_{\\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\\times}}(\\mathrm{Camb}_{c^\\times})\\right|.\n$$\n\nThe conjecture formalizes numerical evidence that the linear and bipartite Coxeter elements are extremal for the sizes of the images of pop-stack operators. The first inequality is consistent with the known comparison between the linear and bipartite cases, while the general assertion remains open.",

  "362660": {
    "mathdb_id": 362660,
    "title": "Gaussoid axioms suffice for CI implication in singly constrained Gaussian DAG models",
    "statement": "Let $\\mathcal{G}$ be a directed acyclic graph (DAG), and let $i \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp j \\mid K$ be a conditional independence statement such that $i \\not\\perp_{\\mathcal{G}} j \\mid K$. Denote by $\\mathcal{M}_{\\mathcal{G}, i \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp j\\mid K}$ the Gaussian model associated with $\\mathcal{G}$ together with this additional conditional independence statement. Let $\\operatorname{global}(\\mathcal{G})$ be the set of global Markov conditional independence statements of $\\mathcal{G}$.\n\n**Gaussoid-axioms sufficiency conjecture.** If $a \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp b \\mid C$ holds for every covariance matrix $\\Sigma \\in \\mathcal{M}_{\\mathcal{G}, i \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp j\\mid K}$, then $a \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp b \\mid C$ is implied by applying the gaussoid axioms to\n\n$$\n\\operatorname{global}(\\mathcal{G}) \\cup \\{i \\perp\\!\\!\\!\\perp j \\mid K\\}.\n$$\n\nThe conjecture is verified in the paper for models involving four random variables, but its validity for arbitrary numbers of variables remains open.",

    "statement": "Let $k$ be a positive integer, let $\\varepsilon_1,\\ldots,\\varepsilon_k$ be nonnegative real numbers satisfying\n\n$$\n\\varepsilon_1+\\cdots+\\varepsilon_k=1,\n$$\n\nand let $G$ be a graph.     "statement": "For an integer $k\\geq 3$, let a graph be **super-minimally $k$-connected** if it is $k$-connected and no proper subgraph is $k$-connected.     "statement": "Let $G$ be a gonality-tight graph with first gonality $k$ for some integer $k$, and let $g$ denote its genus. If $D$ realizes the second gonality, then\n\n$$\n(k-2)\\cdot D\\sim K_G.\n$$\n\nMoreover, for every integer $1\\leq l\\leq k-2$, all divisors realizing the $\\frac{l(l+3)}{2}$-th gonality are linearly equivalent to $l\\cdot D$.\n\nThe conjecture is motivated by a large number of computational examples and predicts that gonality-tight graphs have a rigid genus, gonality sequence, and linear-equivalence structure for divisors realizing selected gonalities.     "statement": "Fix $r\\ge 2$. An $r$-uniform hypergraph, or **$r$-graph**, is a family of $r$-subsets of a vertex set; write $|\\mathcal H|$ for its number of edges.     "title": "The odd square-plane conjecture for transversal difference numbers",
    "statement": "Let $p$ be an odd prime, and set\n\n$$\nG_p=(\\mathbb Z/p^2\\mathbb Z)^2,\\qquad H_p=pG_p.\n$$\n\nFor a transversal $T$ of $G_p/H_p$, write $D(T)=T-T$ and let\n\n$$\n\\delta(G_p,H_p)=\\min_T |D(T)|.\n$$\n\nEvery normalized transversal has the form $T_f=\\{[x]+p[f(x)]:x\\in\\mathbb F_p^2\\}$ for a function $f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p^2$ with $f(0)=0$. For $u,x\\in\\mathbb F_p^2$, define\n\n$$\nc_u(x)=\\frac{[x+u]-[x]-[u]}{p},\\qquad d_u f(x)=f(x+u)-f(x)+c_u(x),\n$$\n\nand $A_u(f)=\\{d_u f(x):x\\in\\mathbb F_p^2\\}$.\n\n**Odd square-plane conjecture.** For every odd prime $p$,\n\n$$\n\\delta\\bigl((\\mathbb Z/p^2\\mathbb Z)^2,p(\\mathbb Z/p^2\\mathbb Z)^2\\bigr)=(2p-1)^2.\n$$\n\nEquivalently, for every function $f:\\mathbb F_p^2\\to\\mathbb F_p^2$,\n\n$$\n\\sum_{u\\in\\mathbb F_p^2}|A_u(f)|\\geq (2p-1)^2.\n$$\n\nThe coordinate box attains $(2p-1)^2$.     "literal_statement": "Let $R(n,k,l)$ denote the number of runs of $k$ of length $l$ over all compositions of $n$, and let $a(1,m)$ be the corresponding two-toned tiling count, interpreted as zero when its second argument is negative. **The run-count formula.** For all $n,k,l$,\n\n$$\nR(n,k,l)=a(1,n-kl)-2a(1,n-(l+1)k)+a(1,n-(l+2)k).\n$$\n\nThis gives an explicit relation between refined run counts in compositions and two-toned tiling numbers; the supplied context does not indicate that the formula is open or conjectural.",

    "literal_statement": "Let $P=(X,\\prec)$ be a finite poset, let $\\operatorname{\\mathcal{E}}(P)$ be its set of linear extensions, and write $e(P)=|\\operatorname{\\mathcal{E}}(P)|$. **The one-third–two-thirds conjecture.** If $P$ is not totally ordered, then there are distinct elements $x,y\\in X$ such that\n\n$$\n\\frac13\\leq \\frac{|\\\\{L\\in\\operatorname{\\mathcal{E}}(P):L(x)<L(y)\\\\}|}{e(P)}\\leq\\frac23.\n$$\n\nThis conjecture is open in full generality, although it is known for several special classes, including posets of width two, where the bounds are tight.",
